_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees`, and
append a dated record to `acknowledgements` saying why.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The record is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges: a commit
SHA written during a PR stops existing when the PR lands, which used to cost
a follow-up commit per acknowledgement. Squashing rewrites history, not
content, so an object id survives it, along with rebases, cherry-picks and
force pushes.
`acknowledgements` is an ordered list of `{ date, note }`, oldest first, and
it is what bounds route 2. Option 2 used to be unbounded: one note string
that only ever grew, so the honest way out stayed available forever and the
audit itself was never read again. Two caps now end that run and force
route 1, whichever comes first:
- 8 acknowledgements. Each one judges its own delta in isolation; the
union of eight of them is not something a ninth reviewer can hold in
their head, and it is the union that decides whether a verdict moved.
- 90 days from the OLDEST record. Drift acknowledged in spring is being
defended by a judgement nobody has revisited.
Both clocks reset the same way: re-verify the audit, bump `Audited commit`,
and delete the entry from this file.

acknowledgements.note: Recorded in the audit itself as v1.19, whose independent pass moved the anchor to 2d07187. Only the test module of redact.rs moves under Code paths: the shared-vectors test also asserts each vector's replacement counts (addresses, tokens, api_keys). The redactor's code above the test module is byte-identical, so the pass's measurements stand. The vectors file and DiagnosticLogRedactorTest, outside Code paths, gain the vectors and counts the pass found missing, and .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo test --lib -- redact::` in the Tauri (Rust) job. No endpoint, filter, DTO, error response or dump entry changes. Verdict PASS.

Under src-tauri/src the Save logs path of section 1 changes (API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md A4, fixed in its v1.16): logs.rs passes each line through the new redact.rs and unpacks rotated .gz files with flate2, and export_logs also reads session.json next to the logs folder for the key to replace; lib.rs gains `mod redact`. The command list is unchanged: export_logs, log_sidecar_stderr and log_sidecar_exit, none taking a path, URL, key or version from the renderer. regex and flate2 were already in the tree, so Cargo.lock gains edges and no crate. check_for_update, download_pending_update, install_pending_update, PendingUpdate, DownloadedUpdate, the channel map and the pubkey are untouched. Verdict stays PASS.

Under src-tauri/src only redact.rs changes (API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md A4, fixed again in its v1.18): the redactor of the Save logs ZIP now writes what DiagnosticLogRedactor writes, the Java lookaround and backtracking done by hand and the token pattern on Java's ASCII classes. It is a pure function of a line, called only from logs.rs, which does not change; the command list, lib.rs and Cargo.toml do not change either, and no crate is added. check_for_update, download_pending_update, install_pending_update, PendingUpdate, DownloadedUpdate, the channel map and the pubkey are untouched. Verdict stays PASS.

Under src-tauri/src only the test module of redact.rs changes (API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md v1.19): its shared-vectors test also asserts each vector's replacement counts. No code outside #[cfg(test)] moves, so the build the updater ships is the same. Verdict stays PASS.

Change under this path, read rather than waved through as a timing tweak. StartupTimingService swapped its reference clock: the anchor for processStartedAt and for every phase's startedAfterProcessMs moved from an Instant.now() taken in the class's own static initialiser to ManagementFactory.getRuntimeMXBean().getStartTime(), with a wall-clock constant recording how much boot had already passed when the class loaded. Section 1 is untouched by it: the diff does not enter StorageContextInitializer, reads or writes no crypto.bin, touches neither the VOXSEC1 format, the DPAPI USER-scope call, the buffer zeroing, the atomic private-permissioned write, nor the constant-time crypto.fingerprint comparison, and adds no path by which any of them could be reached earlier or skipped. The class holds no secret and opens no file. Section 2 holds: CryptoService is not in the diff, and the one place where boot timing and that section intersect - the self-test "warmed off the boot path" claim - is about when the self-test runs, which this change does not move; it only changes what a later dump reports about the time that had already elapsed. The new dependency is java.management, read-only and already in the sidecar's --add-modules list; it is an MXBean read, not a JNI or FFM call, so the "pure Java FFM (no JNI)" hygiene claim of section 1 is about a path this does not join. Section 3 residuals are unaffected - nothing about mail.db plaintext at rest or the same-user-malware exclusion turns on a clock source. The one observable effect outside the boundary is that startup-timings.json in the diagnostic dump now reports a start roughly four seconds earlier and correspondingly larger phase offsets: the same data category as before, no new field and no new value class, and the dump's privacy check is RELEASE_CHECKLIST section 7, which is flagged for a re-take on this candidate for exactly this reason.

Recorded in the audit itself as v1.2: the PBKDF2 iteration count moves from CryptoProperties (mail.crypto.pbkdf2-iterations, @Min 1000, default 600000) to a private constant PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 600_000 in CryptoService, and CryptoProperties.java joins Code paths with this entry, so a format value cannot come back as a property unseen. The bean constructor is now @Autowired and passes the constant to a package-private constructor that takes the count, which CryptoServiceTest uses with 1000; getOrDeriveKey reads the field where it read the property. Section 2 holds with the same values: AES/GCM, 12-byte IV, 128-bit tag, PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 at 600,000 over global salt || accountId to 256 bits, accountId as AAD, the self-test, the LRU and the shutdown hygiene are byte-identical, and a ciphertext pinned in CryptoServiceTest from the production constructor decrypts (changing the constant to 700_000 fails it, run and seen). Section 1 is untouched: core/init and core/security/secret did not change. Verdict stays PASS.

A comment, and nothing else: the two changed lines of MailContentService are the comment on the catch around body extraction. It said the wrapped exception lets MailFacade surface a contentError on the cached body; the message detail no longer calls this service and the field is gone, so it now says the caller gets a typed mail error instead of a 500. The sanitize call, the cid collection, the plain-text escape, the byte cap and the oversize flag are byte-identical, and the body still reaches the frame only through /content, which returns what this service produced. Verdict stays PASS.

The exception-text change of API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md 1.9: a new MailFailureCause enum in the exception package classifies a caught exception into a stable cause code, and MailConnectionException / MailOperationException gained constructors that take the cause and pass the classification, not the text, as the message argument. Under this audit's paths only MailContentService changes, in one line: the failure to extract a message's text passes the caught exception as the cause of its MailOperationException instead of appending its text to the message. What the service extracts, sanitizes or renders is unchanged, so no claim of this audit moves.

Every not-found and validation error names a message key of its own, recorded in API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md as v1.11: ResourceNotFoundException(String) and ValidationException(String), which passed the message as the {0} of a generic key, are removed, and each site that used them names a key. Under this audit's path MailContentService changes in two throws: a message missing from the database names error.message.notFound, and one no longer on the server error.message.goneFromServer. What the service extracts, sanitizes, caps or renders is unchanged, so no claim of this audit moves. Verdict stays PASS.

#689: the body frame's base stylesheet becomes one per text-size step, read against section 3 (Frame -- defense in depth). The claim holds as written: the frame's <meta> CSP is still default-src 'none' with script-src and style-src each pinned to one sha256, base-uri and form-action 'none', the sandbox is still allow-scripts without allow-same-origin, and the forwarder script and its hash are byte-identical. What moved: MAIL_FRAME_STYLE and MAIL_FRAME_STYLE_SHA256 are now tables keyed by small/medium/large, generated from one template whose only variable is the frame's root font size (15/16/18px from stores/textSize.ts); the body's 14px became 0.875rem; mailFrameCsp(loadRemoteImages, textSize) names the hash of the one step it is given, so a frame admits its own style and not the other two; MessageContent.svelte passes the current text size to buildMailFrameSrcdoc and is otherwise unchanged. The 'recompute the CSP hashes' method note still applies, three times: the three hashes were derived from the generated strings with SHA-256/base64 and match, and mailFrame.test.ts recomputes them. No sanitizer, remote-image, link-relay or height-relay code changed. Verdict unchanged.

The forwarder's preventDefault predicate gains Ctrl+Y, read against section 3 (Frame -- defense in depth). The app claims Ctrl+Y for the workspace pane since #687, and the predicate is meant to mirror what handleGlobalKeydown claims, so the genuine keystroke in the frame is cancelled as Ctrl+R and Ctrl+P are; the letter class /^[kprfqu]$/i became /^[kprfquy]$/i and nothing else in the script moved. Cancelling a default grants the frame nothing: what it posts out is unchanged (every isTrusted keydown was already relayed), and so are the link relay and the height relay. MAIL_FRAME_SCRIPT_SHA256 was recomputed from the new string with SHA-256/base64 and mailFrame.test.ts recomputes it; the CSP still pins script-src to that one hash, the sandbox is still allow-scripts without allow-same-origin. Under message-detail, MessageHeaderCard.svelte adds min-h-0 to the class of the inline address link, a layout change only. No sanitizer or remote-image code changed. Verdict unchanged.

The residual of 1.40 in section 4e (a second copy of the draft after a rejected save), fixed and recorded in the audit itself as v1.68; functional, so no claim of a finding moves and the anchor stays at 6ff9ded. Two paths move. DraftRecipientsRepository gains findEarlierRevisions, a read: the stableIds of the account's entries in the chain of a given stableId written before it by saved_seq, empty when that stableId has no entry. Under feature/mail/service only DraftPersistenceService changes: saveDraftAsync resolves, before the APPEND as before, the named revision's row and the rows of the chain's earlier revisions (replacedRevisions, earlierRevisionRows), each through isReplaceableDraft, and after a stored APPEND hard-deletes each and its row; deleteSupersededDraft does the same for the draft a send supersedes and also sets aside each deleted revision's entry, as it does the named one's. No entry is deleted or written by the new code, so 1.58's claim that entries go only by the two bounds holds; DraftPersistenceServiceTest still pins that the save and the send touch the repository only to read, besides the send's set-aside. The guard, the APPEND, markStored and the recipient check are unchanged.

Schema housekeeping, no claim of a finding moves and the anchor stays at 6ff9ded. One path moves: MessageEntity gains bodyText, mapped to the new messages.body_text column, and setContent now sets it to BodyText.of(content) (jsoup text() of the cached HTML, null exactly when content is). message_search and its triggers read body_text instead of content, so the index holds the visible text of a body rather than its markup; nothing else reads the column. MessageContentPersister is still the only production caller of setContent, and nothing writes body_text on its own, so B1-1's claim that content stays NULL for an oversized body, and the index with it never sees a placeholder, holds for body_text too. For the informational note on thread renumbering in section 5: the managed entities it loads now carry body_text as well, which is no longer than content (text() only drops markup and decodes entities) and null for a message nobody has opened, so the note's worst case stays an opened long thread and the body text each loaded entity holds at most doubles; the note's 'not measured' stands. V1__init.sql also moves the long text columns of messages to the end of the row, which no audited path depends on.

Under this audit's paths only application.properties changes: two keys, mail.client.db.checkpoint-initial-delay=PT1M and mail.client.db.checkpoint-interval=PT5M, schedule a WAL checkpoint pass (PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)) in DatabaseMaintenanceService, which is in core/maintenance, outside this audit's paths. No mail.client.imap.*, mail.client.sync.* or SMTP key moves, so no bound a finding rests on changes. PASSIVE waits on no reader or writer, so the sync's write transactions are neither blocked nor failed by it.

Under this audit's paths only application.properties changes: mail.crypto.pbkdf2-iterations=600000 is removed, because the count is now a constant in CryptoService (CRYPTO_STORAGE_AUDIT.md v1.2), and the comment above the crypto keys names it among the format constants. No mail.client.imap.*, mail.client.sync.* or SMTP key moves, so no bound a finding rests on changes. Verdict unchanged.

A javadoc in SecurityConfig.pkceAuthorizationRequestResolver now names client_secret_basic, Spring's default for the google registration, where it said client_secret_post (OAUTH_AUDIT.md section 4 note). Comment only: the filter chain, PKCE, CORS and the handlers are unchanged. Verdict unchanged.

Two section 4 notes acted on, recorded in the audit itself as v1.6. ExternalProviderLoginService: findOrCreateExternalAccount still looks up (oauth2_provider, external_id) first, then the address, but the address now takes only a row with no oauth2_provider and no external_id (the password upgrade the fallback was written for); a row another identity owns makes the sign-in throw AccountAlreadyExistsException (409, error.account.alreadyExists) before any write, so the row, its binding and its token stay as they are, inside the same transaction that rolls back. markRequiresReauthIfExists takes (providerName, externalId, reason) and finds the account by findByOauth2ProviderAndExternalId instead of findByEmail, and the audit line carries the reason. Under feature/auth only OAuth2LoginService changes: its two callers pass providerName, externalId (validated non-blank by the guard before them) and missing_refresh_token or missing_scope. The four guards, their order, the flag's one clearing path, PKCE, the redirect handling, the session end at /success and the token storage are untouched. What moves narrows what a sign-in may touch: an account another identity owns can no longer be re-bound or flagged by it. Verdict stays PASS.

auth-finished.html and auth-failed.html, the pages the system browser shows after a sign-in, change for WCAG 2.2 only: the English half of each is marked lang="en" (3.1.2), the reason line on the failure page is #4b5563 instead of #6b7280 on #f3f4f6 (4.39:1 to 1.4.3's 4.5:1), and its Czech text uses the en dash. Markup and CSS only: the inline script that writes ?reason= with textContent, the redirect targets and the public-endpoint list are unchanged. Verdict unchanged.
